findings.finding: Shurgard's Q3 2026 release (11 Nov) says its UK business improved over Jul-Sep: same-store revenue turned positive at +0.8% after a decline in H1, occupancy at 87.4% was +0.5ppt year on year, and rental-rate pressure eased (-0.2% against -0.6% in H1). That is a direct-competitor read for the quarter Big Yellow has not yet reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Occupancy is the line Big Yellow trades on, and the stock has fallen on it: -4.85% the day after the Nov 2024 interims and -2.05% after the May 2026 finals. Interims of 17 Nov 2025 were flat (0.0%) during the Blackstone situation.
findings.original_quote: United Kingdom: our performance in that market improved during the third quarter, as a result of stronger occupancy across both the same-store and non-same-store segments... Same store revenue growth turned positive with +0.8% in Q3, compared to a decline in H1.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a Brussels-listed peer's release from two sessions ago, and BYG barely moved on it (+0.53% on 11/10, -0.05% on 11/11, -1.26% on 11/12). Shurgard's UK estate is more regional than Big Yellow's London-weighted one, so it is a proxy and sized small. If it were priced as a read for BYG, the stock would have re-rated over 11-12 Nov.
findings.independence: Safestore's Q3 to 31 July showed UK LFL revenue +1.9% and UK average rate +4.6% (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/safestore-holdings--safe/third-quarter-trading-update/9752862). Its period ends a month earlier and it cut group EPS to the lower half of the range, so it supports demand but not margin.

findings.finding: On the company's own numbers the Q2 comparison is easy. Last year Q2 lost about 75k sq ft (H1 -28k against Q1 +47k) and closed September at 5,028k sq ft with LFL occupancy at 78.2%. Q1 2026 had already reached 5,146k (+161k in the quarter), so even a flat Q2 gives about +2.3% occupied space year on year at the half, which would be the first positive year-on-year half-year occupancy since 2023.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims (LFL occupancy -2.3ppt yoy, 'modest improvement' since): 0.0%. Nov 2024 interims: -4.85%. Q1 statement Jul 2026 (+161k sq ft): -1.08% next session.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: fifteen analysts can do this arithmetic, which is why it is sized at +0.2. What is not known is the actual Q2 net let-up; peak-season moves of plus or minus 75k sq ft are possible. If the arithmetic were fully trusted, the stock would not have fallen on the Q1 statement that already showed the gain.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 figures: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/big-yellow-group--byg/q1-trading-statement/9675717. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: The company guided a first-half like-for-like store opex rise of 4%, against -2% in last year's H1, and is funding a GBP212m pipeline. Last year's H1 EPRA EPS growth of +7% to 30.0p was built on cost savings and lower interest that will not repeat, so H1 EPRA EPS is likely flat to slightly down. This is inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 finals (18 May 2026, adjusted EPS +2%, dividend +2%): -2.05% next session.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced because the company told the market in July, so it sits near zero. It stays filed because the EPS comparison against 30.0p will be the headline wire line.

findings.finding: The stock has rallied from 799p (13 Oct) to 947.5p on the Ancora (>4%, intrinsic value 1,236p) and Irenic (~4%) campaigns for a sale. The board's only response (15 Oct) said it will 'continue to focus on executing the Company's clear and proven strategy', and these interims are its first full statement since. A standalone restatement under the new CEO would put part of that premium at risk; a formal review would be a large upside tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Strategic and bid news is the line that has really moved this stock: +15.44% on 13 Oct 2025 (Blackstone), -6.38% on 1 Dec 2025 and -4.30% on 5 Dec 2025 as talks ended, +5.38% and +5.05% on 14-15 Oct 2026 (activists).
findings.original_quote: The Board and management team continue to focus on executing the Company's clear and proven strategy. The Board is also cognisant of its fiduciary duties and continually evaluates all options for maximising shareholder value.
findings.why_not_priced: The price holds an option on a sale (about +19% since 13 Oct, run_up_20d +5.0%) but cannot know which way the board will lean in the release. The board's own last wording leans standalone. If the market were pricing the standalone outcome, the stock would have given back the activist move instead of extending it to 950-967p in early November.
findings.independence: Ancora's call and price (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/ancora-calls-materially-undervalued-big-yellow-consider-sale, 2026-10-13) and Irenic's ~4% stake (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/update-2nd-activist-shareholder-pushes-big-yellow-explore-sale, 2026-10-16).

findings.finding: Three industrial-estate disposals raise GBP81m of gross proceeds. The company says this funds this year's and next year's capex 'without materially increasing absolute levels of debt' and takes net debt/EBITDA from about 3.7x toward its 3.5x target. The money buys a 12-store pipeline guided at a 16.5% return on the GBP212m cost to complete, and it also gives room for the capital return the activists want.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Disposal days: Staines (15 Sep 2026) and Bracknell (23 Sep 2026) did not visibly move the stock; no measured reaction on this line.
findings.original_quote: We are largely able to fund our capital expenditure this year and next from capital receipts and retained cash flow, without materially increasing absolute levels of debt.
findings.why_not_priced: The disposals are public. What is not public is whether the interims turn the proceeds into a buyback or a lower development commitment; that line carries the size.

language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: the domestic RNS record on Investegate (issuer timing notice, Q1 statement, disposals, TR-1s, last year's interims) was the primary source for the facts, and the same facts were carried by the English wire and retail-platform copy (AJ Bell/Alliance News, HL). lessons_applied: coverage band >13: the Q2 comparison arithmetic is something fifteen analysts can compute, so that finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2
a narrow proxy loses to a broad series / macro-to-company is a hypothesis: the Shurgard UK read was cut from +0.4 to +0.3 (regional estate against London-weighted BYG)
understatement is the systematic error and the move lives in what is new: abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.0 because Q2 and H1 are not pre-released and the strategic line carries a tail
the reaction history vetoes direction, not size: results sold on 5 of 6 recent days moved p_up from 49 to 48, and abs_move_pct was left alone
'in a live bid, results are noise' checked: BYG is not in an offer period (no Rule 2.4 or Form 8 since Dec 2025), so the strategic line stays one finding rather than the whole answer
